limitations: The finding is static and does not establish runtime reachability.
Without explicit interprocedural alias and ordering evidence, source matches do not prove that the settings affect the WebView that renders the data or remain enabled at render time.
The detector does not prove that the HTML is externally controlled, mutable, contains executable script, or executes JavaScript.
The detector does not prove that a readable sensitive resource exists, that access succeeds, or that information is disclosed.
CWE-200 describes a possible confidentiality impact category; it is not proof of an exploit or necessarily the most specific root-cause classification.
predicates: A WebSettings configuration enables universal access from file URLs.
The relevant settings are associated with the WebView used for rendering.
A WebView.loadDataWithBaseURL call uses a base URL that evaluates to a file:// URL.
For an actual security issue, the rendered data must be less trusted or executable in a way that permits JavaScript to run; this provenance is not established solely by the configuration pattern.
detector_semantics.claim: A potentially dangerous static combination exists when a JavaScript-enabled WebView is configured with allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs=true and renders data through loadDataWithBaseURL using a file:// base URL.

unknowns: No governed API type named WebViewFileAccessSpec is identified or assumed; the specification names a concern rather than an Android API type.
The supplied finding does not provide the detector implementation or a rule catalog, so its precise alias, data-flow, ordering, and trust-provenance analysis is unresolved.
The exact runtime origin classification and file-access behavior of HTML supplied to loadDataWithBaseURL with a file:// base URL require version-specific Android System WebView evidence.
Whether the rendered HTML is downloaded, externally modifiable, attacker-controlled, or script-capable requires application-specific data-flow evidence.
Whether any local or cross-origin readable resource is sensitive, and whether it reaches an unauthorized actor, is unresolved.

documented_behavior: android.webkit.WebSettings.setJavaScriptEnabled(true) enables JavaScript execution in a WebView; the documented default is false.

android.webkit.WebSettings.setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true) allows cross-origin requests from a file-scheme URL context to access content from any origin, including other file URLs. Android documents this setting as insecure and deprecated beginning with API level 30.

android.webkit.WebView.loadDataWithBaseURL(baseUrl, data, mimeType, encoding, historyUrl) renders supplied data and uses baseUrl for relative-URL resolution and JavaScript same-origin-policy behavior.

Android documentation states that content supplied through loadDataWithBaseURL can access local device files through file-scheme URLs only when baseUrl uses a scheme other than http, https, ftp, ftps, about, or javascript.
preconditions: setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs is available from Android API level 16.
Universal access from file URLs applies to JavaScript running in a file-scheme URL context.
JavaScript must be enabled and actually execute for script-based reads to occur.
The setting writes and rendering operation must affect the same live WebView instance.
A requested resource must be reachable and readable under the application sandbox, WebView configuration, platform behavior, and resource-specific protections.
unknowns: The API references do not resolve for every Android System WebView version whether data loaded with a file:// base URL satisfies the exact file-scheme execution-context predicate of setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs.
The effect of other WebSettings, including setAllowFileAccess and later configuration changes, is not established by this finding.
The API documentation does not establish the trust provenance or mutability of the data argument.
Actual behavior can depend on the installed Android System WebView/Chromium implementation and device API level.

events.condition: Observation: a WebSettings setter call or Kotlin property assignment enabling JavaScript is present. Predicate: the enabled value must be effective on the same WebView before the rendered document attempts to execute script.
events.name: enable_javascript

events.condition: Observation: a WebSettings setter call or Kotlin property assignment with true is present. Predicate: it must be effective for the same WebView when JavaScript executes in a file-scheme URL context.
events.name: enable_universal_access_from_file_urls

events.condition: Observation: a WebView.loadDataWithBaseURL call is present, optionally with a nearby file:// literal. Predicate: the baseUrl must evaluate to a file-scheme URL, the data must be script-capable rendered content, and the invocation must target the WebView whose effective settings satisfy the preceding predicates.
events.name: render_data_with_file_base

important_note: This specification describes a static configuration concern, not a demonstrated disclosure. The documented setting permits JavaScript in a file-scheme context to make cross-origin requests, including to other file URLs. A finding alone does not establish that the calls execute, affect one WebView, remain enabled, render attacker-controlled or script-bearing content, expose a sensitive readable resource, or disclose data. CWE-200 is a high-level resultant exposure category and MITRE marks it as discouraged for real-world vulnerability mapping.
forbidden_inferences_without_evidence: That the configuration calls execute on a reachable runtime path.
That JavaScript and universal-access settings apply to the same WebView instance used by loadDataWithBaseURL.
That these settings remain enabled at rendering time; later writes can change the effective values.
That the data passed to loadDataWithBaseURL is downloaded, externally alterable, or attacker-controlled.
That rendered data contains script, has an injection point, or successfully executes JavaScript.
That a file-scheme base passed to loadDataWithBaseURL is treated as the required file-scheme JavaScript context on the deployed Android System WebView version.
That local file access is otherwise enabled or that a particular sensitive local resource is readable by the WebView or application sandbox.
That a network response, another origin's response, cookies, app-private data, credentials, or another particular secret can be read.
That data was exfiltrated, displayed to an unauthorized party, or otherwise disclosed.
That CWE-200 is the most specific or appropriate final CWE mapping for a confirmed issue.

security_semantics.runtime_claim: A runtime confidentiality issue requires effective settings on the rendering WebView, JavaScript execution by less-trusted content in the necessary file-related context, successful reading of a resource that should not be available to that content, and an unauthorized observation or transfer of that resource.
security_semantics.detector_claim: The static combination is a candidate for file-based cross-origin access by JavaScript in rendered HTML and therefore a possible confidentiality exposure.

compatibility: Device API level must be at least 16 for setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs.
API level 30 or later marks the method deprecated; deprecation alone does not establish its runtime effect.
Application target SDK and Android version can affect defaults for related settings, especially setAllowFileAccess; explicit writes and final effective values remain material.
The installed Android System WebView/Chromium version should be recorded because file-origin and request behavior can vary by implementation.
runtime: A reachable execution path configures and renders the same WebView in the required order.
Runtime values confirm JavaScript enabled, allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs, and other relevant file-access settings.
Runtime testing confirms the resulting document URL/origin behavior for the deployed Android System WebView.
Controlled evidence shows that script in rendered content can read an in-scope resource that should not be exposed to that content.
Evidence establishes unauthorized observation, transmission, or another disclosure if asserting confidentiality impact.
source_level: A source-level association connects the WebView used by loadDataWithBaseURL to its WebSettings instance.
Evidence shows that setJavaScriptEnabled(true) and setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true) are effective rather than overwritten later.
Evidence shows that the loadDataWithBaseURL baseUrl argument evaluates to a file:// URL.
Evidence establishes the provenance, integrity, and mutability of the data argument.
Evidence shows that rendered data is HTML or another format capable of executing JavaScript.

name: WebViewFileAccessSpec
semantic_scope: For every finding of this rule, the detector reports a static, non-executed candidate based on a WebView configuration-and-rendering relationship: JavaScript is enabled, universal cross-origin access from file URLs is enabled, and data is rendered through loadDataWithBaseURL using a file:// base URL. The concern is that script in externally sourced or otherwise less-trusted rendered HTML may execute with file-related privileges broad enough to read local or cross-origin content, creating a potential confidentiality impact. The rule observes source-level configuration and call-flow indicators; it does not establish runtime reachability, content trust, script execution, resource readability, or disclosure.
known_false_positive_shapes: The identified setters and loadDataWithBaseURL call operate on different WebView or WebSettings objects.
The code is unreachable, feature-gated, exception-terminated, or present only on a non-executed lifecycle path.
A later configuration call disables JavaScript or universal file-URL access before rendering.
The base URL is computed at runtime and does not resolve to file:// on the relevant path.
The rendered HTML is fixed application-controlled content, cannot be altered by an external actor, and has no script injection or executable untrusted-content path.
The rendered document has no executable script and no route by which external input becomes executable script.
A file-access restriction, platform restriction, sandbox boundary, or resource permission prevents reading the alleged target.
The deployed Android System WebView treats the loadDataWithBaseURL document differently from the assumed file-scheme JavaScript context.
No sensitive resource is readable within the application/WebView scope, or no unauthorized recipient can receive data.
protocol: WebView.getSettings() -> setJavaScriptEnabled(true) AND setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true) -> loadDataWithBaseURL(file://..., HTML, ...) -> [only if executable less-trusted HTML runs in an applicable file-scheme context and reads an accessible resource] potential disclosure

detector_examples.message: Static candidate (not executed): onCreate sets allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs = true on a JavaScript-enabled WebView that renders downloaded What If article HTML with loadDataWithBaseURL("file:///android_asset/.", ...), so script in that remote HTML runs with a file:// origin that may read local files and any other origin (CWE-200).
